title: Count Special Quadruplets
statement: You are given an integer array `nums` indexed from 0. Count the index quadruplets `(a, b, c, d)` with `a < b < c < d` for which the values at the first three indices add up to the value at the last one, that is `nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] == nums[d]`, and return that count. Two quadruplets are different when they differ in at least one index, even if the values are the same.
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 50 numbers, trying every quadruplet in four nested loops already passes, but it costs O(n⁴). Move `nums[c]` to the other side: the rule becomes `nums[a] + nums[b] == nums[d] - nums[c]`. Now the left pair sits entirely before `c` and the right pair entirely from `c` on, so if we know how often each difference `nums[d] - nums[c]` occurs among pairs to the right of `b`, every `(a, b)` pair can be answered with one map lookup.

## Approach

1. Walk `b` from `n - 3` down to `1`, keeping `diffCount`: how many pairs `(c, d)` with `b < c < d` have each difference `nums[d] - nums[c]`.
2. When `b` moves one step left, exactly one new `c` becomes valid, `c = b + 1`. Add the differences of all its pairs `(c, d)` to `diffCount`.
3. For every `a < b`, add `diffCount.get(nums[a] + nums[b])` to `count` (zero when missing).
4. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3, 6]`, so `n = 4` and `b` only takes the value `1`. Then `c = 2`, and the only `d` is `3`: `diff = 6 - 3 = 3`, so `diffCount = {3: 1}`. For `a = 0`, `nums[0] + nums[1] = 3` is in the map once, so `count` becomes `1`, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each `b` adds at most n differences and scans at most n values of `a`.
- Space: O(n²) at most for the keys of `diffCount`, and here never more than 199 keys, since every difference lies between -99 and 99.

## Pitfalls

- Index order matters: the map may only hold pairs with `c > b`, which is why `b` walks right to left and adds `c = b + 1` before using the map.
- Count index quadruplets, not distinct value sets: equal values at different positions are separate quadruplets.
- A missing key must count as 0, not `undefined`, or `count` becomes `NaN`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `diffCount` | map from `nums[d] - nums[c]` to how many pairs `(c, d)` right of `b` give it |
| `count` | quadruplets found so far |
| `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` | the four indices, with `a < b < c < d` |
| `diff` | the difference `nums[d] - nums[c]` of the pair being added |

narration.3: The map counts, for each difference nums[d] - nums[c], how many pairs to the right of b produce it.
narration.6: Walk b from right to left so the set of allowed (c, d) pairs only grows.
narration.7: Moving b one step left makes exactly one new c available, the index right after b.
narration.8: Pair the new c with every d after it.
narration.10: Record this difference; a pair (a, b) whose sum equals it completes a quadruplet.
narration.12: Now try every a before b.
narration.13: nums[a] + nums[b] must equal nums[d] - nums[c], so add how many stored pairs have that difference.
narration.16: Every quadruplet was counted exactly once, at its own b; return the total.
